_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band4_upper_meadows_ironwood. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 4000-4999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

clusters.name: ridge_patrol_camp
clusters._why: GATE-D4/prompt 65: spec Band 4 names 'ruined watch/occupation traces' and 'Team Tether patrol camps' among the region's regional identity and this band had zero prop clusters authored at package start. Sited on the watchtower spur beside the new patrol trainer (trainers.json order 4000) and 46m from captain_ridge -- the garrison the trainer belongs to, read the same way `old_quarry.gd`'s `quarry_station` and `ranger_camp` clusters read their own sites: a posting left mid-shift, not a stage set. Same prop family both of those already use (D24, one prop family) -- nothing here is new. A crate and barrel for supply, a bag and rope for gear, a whetstone for the same reason the quarry crew left one, and the axe standing in for a Team Tether tool rather than a mining one: the composition differs by what a patrol carries, not by a new mesh.

props._why: the post's own supply crate, set where a picket would actually stack one -- against the ruin, not in the open
water for a posting nowhere near the river -- set touching the crate, one load rather than a scatter
a picket's kit, dropped rather than packed -- the same detail that reads 'abandoned' at the quarry and the ranger camp, told a third time
coiled beside the crate -- what tied a watch-line to the ruin above before the ruin stopped being watched
set down and not picked back up, same reasoning as the quarry crew's own whetstone -- someone left in a hurry, not on schedule
leaning against the crate, pitched off vertical -- the one tool that names a patrol rather than a dig, the same lean `quarry_station`'s pickaxe uses for the same reason

SITE-DRESSING: the D1 trail-camp's own solved fire (Bonfire_Fire.obj's real `Fire` surface + ignite() + campfire_glow.gd's light/embers/smoke), scaled down further than band1's -- a patrol posting keeps a smaller fire than a rest camp. Sited past the crate/bag pile on the open side of the ruin, the ground a critic reading this as 'barrel/crate/bench on virgin grass' has nothing standing on.

SITE-DRESSING: the D1 fire-ring mesh (owner-referenced, already committed under assets/props/generated_camp -- no new generation), scaled to this smaller fire's own footprint the same way band1 matched it to its six-stone predecessor.
SITE-DRESSING: one seat, facing the fire across it -- the piece that turns a fire into a place someone sits rather than a lit prop. Same model band1's trail_camp already uses for its own second seat.

SITE-DRESSING: the D1 owner-referenced tent mesh (already committed, no new generation), scaled down from band1's 1.05 -- a patrol keeps one small shelter, not a rest camp's. Placed against the ruin behind the crate/barrel, mouth turned toward the fire so the tent and the fire read as one posting instead of two unrelated objects. `sink_m` copied from band1's own measured fix for this same mesh's raised local origin.

SITE-DRESSING: first of three stepping stones on the south-west approach (the capture viewpoint's own eye line, tools/_capture_band4_sites.gd `ridge-patrol-camp`) -- ground props.gd/vegetation.json cannot touch a worn-path texture, so the beaten route reads as a line of trodden stone instead. Same Rock_Medium family band1's own fire-ring arc uses; a rotation/scale distinct from its two siblings below so the line does not repeat one stone three times.
SITE-DRESSING: second stepping stone, midway between the approach and the fire.
SITE-DRESSING: third stepping stone, closing the line onto the camp's own supply pile -- the arriving path connection the ridge camp had none of.
